title: The race detector (`-race`): running it, reading the output and fixing it

videos.script: Every lesson so far has written goroutines. This one checks them. The race detector is the one tool in this course you cannot learn by reading about it, so this lesson is almost all running it. {{cost}} First, what it is. A second build of your program, where every memory access is checked. You measure the price on one program: twelve times slower, nine times the memory. That price decides where it runs. {{report}} Then a report, read line by line. Two accesses and two birthplaces. Lines 17 and 22 of a small program, and the go statement on line 15. {{fixes}} Next, three races and three different fixes. An atomic for one number. A mutex for a map. And for a slice, no lock at all: each goroutine gets its own slot. {{test}} Last, the race no program shows you. A cache that passes its tests six times, and fails the moment the detector watches. {{close}} That closes the concurrency half. Lesson 17 starts the standard library.
